newsitem.title: USA: Dole takes center stage at White House.
newsitem.headline: Dole takes center stage at White House.

text.p: It was what Bob Dole has been wanting for years: to take centre stage in the White House East Room with "Hail to the Chief" playing, all eyes on him as he stepped to the podium with the presidential seal.
Acting like he was taking the coveted oath of office, he declared: "I, Robert J. Dole... do solemnly swear..."
He paused. Gales of laughter swept the historic room. President Bill Clinton doubled over with merriment. Dole deadpanned: "Sorry, wrong speech."
Then he added to even more laughter: "I had a dream ... that I would be here this historic week receiving something from the president -- but I thought it would be the front-door key."
President Clinton on Friday bestowed America's highest civilian award, the Presidential Medal of Freedom, on Dole, the Republican he defeated to win a second term on Nov. 5.

Since the election Clinton had been wanting to honour Dole's service as a disabled hero of World War Two and his 35 years in Congress, feeling that Dole did not get proper recognition when he resigned from the Senate last May because it came during the heat of the campaign.
Aides said Clinton had great respect for Dole even though he disagreed with the Republican's politics.

Clinton hailed Dole's work on behalf of farmers in his home state of Kansas, his work for the disabled, after having had his right arm disabled in the war, and his support for voting rights and for preserving Social Security.
"Son of the soil, citizen, soldier and legislator, Bob Dole understands the American people, their struggles, their triumphs and their dreams," he said.
